grh_4443c84ca65c52d06227.title: The Pirate Of Rivers End
paragraphs: A local historian's new manuscript about Rivers End begins exposing facts that respectable families would rather forget. Mrs. Sherman comes to Dr. Christian because wealthy Oscar Duban has learned that her son Brett was adopted and that Brett's natural father served time in prison. Duban uses the discovery to oppose Brett's engagement to his daughter Elaine, and Mrs. Sherman desperately asks Christian to conceal or falsify the truth. Christian refuses. Elaine, however, already knows Brett was adopted and still intends to marry him; Brett is proud of the parents who chose and raised him. Christian then turns the historian's research on Duban himself and discovers that the Duban fortune traces back to a notorious French pirate whose stolen property became the foundation of the family's standing. Faced with his own ancestry, Duban must admit that a person should not be judged by an ancestor's crimes. He drops his objection and gives Elaine and Brett permission to marry.

grh_44147d653a4b666c36dc.title: The Odyssey of the Vigilant
paragraphs: The surveillance ship Vigilant encounters an unknown craft and its crew vanishes, leaving Captain Adam Bricker, Lieutenant Eve Kramer and Chief Stone prisoners of an alien power. Their captors, the Alveons, kill the rest of the crew and select the three humans as expendable warriors in a campaign against the Zaborians. After a failed escape, the prisoners are sent into battle, where Chief Stone reveals that he is descended from refugees who escaped a world the Alveons destroyed thousands of years earlier, making Adam and Eve descendants of his people. Stone dies helping defeat their enemies, and the Alveons, satisfied with the result, allow Adam and Eve either to return home or remain on the small planet where the battle occurred. They choose to stay, name the world Earth after the ancestral planet that was destroyed, and become the implied beginning of a new human population there.

grh_44ba1c4745cfabe2e46e.title: The Girl With The Golden Gauntlets
paragraphs: Dr. Christian remembers Paris before the war, when his wealthy, aimless friend Steve became infatuated with the celebrated beauty Ariella, famous for never removing long golden gloves. Suspicious of her reputation and curious about the secret beneath the gloves, Steve and Dr. Christian trick Ariella into exposing hands that are badly deformed. Horrified by the cruelty of what he has done, Steve abandons his idle life and devotes himself to medicine, becoming a renowned plastic surgeon. Years later Dr. Christian reveals that the glamorous woman visiting Rivers End is Ariella herself, now Steve's wife, and that Steve's career was driven by his determination to restore the hands he once shamed her for hiding.
